necessity_findings.reason: Pain persisted 6+ weeks or red flags present.

retrieved.text: Routine MRI of the lumbar spine is not indicated for acute uncomplicated low back pain lasting under 6 weeks without documented red-flag features.

Lumbar spine MRI is indicated for low back pain accompanied by documented red-flag features (severe or progressive neurological deficit, suspected cauda equina syndrome, suspected spinal infection, or malignancy), or when persistent pain lasts 6 weeks or more despite documented adherence to conservative therapy (physiotherapy, medication).

Knee arthroscopy is indicated for meniscal tears with persistent mechanical symptoms (joint locking, catching, or giving way) after at least 6 weeks of failed conservative care; it is not indicated for degenerative osteoarthritis alone in the absence of mechanical obstruction.
Knee MRI is indicated for persistent knee pain lasting 6 weeks or more despite documented conservative management, or immediately following acute severe knee trauma with inability to bear weight.
